messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert — elevated 502/504 errors and timeouts for /v1/embeddings in prod-east-1
Summary: 6x error rate vs baseline over last 3m. Latency spikes at edge and p50 token timeouts. Dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/embeddings?range=3m

oncall-alex: Ack. paging SRE. I'm dropping into the runbook.

sre-jordan: looking — saw a spike in upstream queue length on embedding workers. KV cache pressure, and a small set of clients are sending huge batch sizes (50k tokens/req). Suspect client spike causing worker OOMs.

prod-eng-maya: if it's oversized batches we can do quick per-route throttles. Can we lower the per-request token limit for embeddings and add stricter per-account rte limits? Would prefer config change over full rollback.

oncall-alex: Agreed. Support impact: support-luis, are customers complaining? any high-sev?

support-luis: Yes — 3 customers (acct: brightai, convoflow, datahub-inc) reported 504s and retry storms. CS on patching clients. They're asking for ETA.

prod-eng-maya: Proposed live mitigations (fast path):
1) Apply per-route rate limit for /v1/embeddings: global soft limit 30 rps, per-account 5 rps burst 15
2) Enforce per-request token cap at 8k tokens (reject with 413 if > cap)
3) Temporarily tighten rerank route to 20 rps to preserve throughput for chat
4) Enable aggressive KV cache eviction for embeddings cache TTL -> 30s

sre-jordan: +1. I'll roll limits and watch error surface. Running command now:

```
# apply route-level limits
infractl config set-rate-limit --route "/v1/embeddings" --global-requests-per-second 30 --per-account-rps 5 --burst 15 --reason "mitigate runaway embedding batches"
infractl config set-request-cap --route "/v1/embeddings" --max-tokens 8000
infractl config set-rate-limit --route "/v1/rerank" --global-requests-per-second 20 --reason "preserve compute for chat"
```

deploy-bot: Applying config changes to prod-east-1 -> OK (job id: cfg-2026-03-15-91). Changes live in 12s.

sre-jordan: Watching metrics — dropping 502s within 40s of rollout. Queue len down ~70%.

oncall-alex: Nice. support-luis please ping the 3 customers with short note: mitigation in place, we expect normal traffic in <1h. Offer to bump quota temporarily if they need.

support-luis: Will send now. quick note drafted:
"We're seeing elevated embedding errors earlier. We applied temporary per-route limits and a token cap to stabilize service. No data loss. Full service expected in <1h. If you need a quota bump, reply here and we'll prioritize."

customer-success-anna: Also log the affected accounts and mark for priority review in next 24h.

sre-jordan: Small follow-up: we saw one noisy client IP that retried aggressively. Creating block rule for that IP range for 30m and flagging for mitigation team.

prod-eng-maya: Can we add a per-route circuit-breaker to fail fast for oversized batches? I'll create a PR after incident.

oncall-bella: taking follow-up for next hour — oncall handoff in 10m. Alex, handoff notes?

oncall-alex: Handoff: mitigation applied, metrics stable but still elevated compared to baseline. Watch embedding 5xx rate and queue length. PR from prod-eng to follow for per-request circuit-breaker. Support has notified customers. If errors spike back, rollback limits to earlier values and escalate to infra-leads.

oncall-bella: Ack. I'll take it.

sre-jordan: postmortem stub opened: https://pm.internal.redwood/incidents/1905054321 — will fill root cause (client batch sizes + insufficient per-route caps)

prod-eng-maya: follow-ups:
- enforce default per-request token cap on hosted API (prod config)
- add per-route default rate-limit templates (embeddings heavy workloads)
- improve observability: split error reasons for 5xx vs client rejection (413)

support-luis: Customers updated — two replied asking for temporary quota increases; will coordinate with billing/ops.

incident-bot: Incident state moved -> mitigated by oncall-alex

oncall-bella: I'll keep an eye for next 60m then do final wrap. Thanks team :thumbsup:
